newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power firm as mild temps stay.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power firm as mild temps stay.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. remained firm Wednesday as mild temperatures were predicted to stay in the region slightly longer than expected.
"Everyone is holding their own," said a Florida trader, adding trading activity was light today.
Revised forecasts showed cold weather would not reach the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) until this weekend rather than Thursday or Friday as previously expected.

Some participants said they seeked to move power from SERC to northern districts such as Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) and East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) because of rising spot prices there due to cold weather and tight generation capacity.
Electricity for next-day delivery from South Carolina to Wisconsin reportedly changed hands in the $29.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
For Thursday, temperatures in SERC were expected to peak in 40s-70s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 30s-50s, while those in Florida were predicted to peak in the 50s-60s and bottom in the 30s-50s.
Reduced transmission capacity at the Georgia-Florida interface for Thursday deliveries kept next-day power prices firm in the pennisula.
Among Florida utilities, 12-hour block power for Thursday delivery was quoted in the $27.00-$29.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Thursday was still valued at $21.00-$23.00, while 12-hour blocks was talked at $17.00-$18.00.
Firm, off-peak Ga./Fla. power deliveries for Thursday were assessed at $17.00-$18.00, unchanged from Tuesday's range.
Peak, firm electricity for Thursday delivery into northwestern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory was again assessed at $17.00-$18.00.
Firm deliveries during light-load hours on Thursday held steady at $13.00-$15.00.
TVA itself was heard offering next-day power during heavy load hours in the low-$20.00's level, up from Tuesday's $19.50 area, and during light load hours near $16.00 even with Tuesday.
TVA's Sequoyah 1 nuclear power unit in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn., continued to hold output at 55 percent of its 1,148 megawatt (MW) capacity following a weekend outage.
